question: Which exact P65 app/launcher/LVX API candidates could support a Canopus Manager backend, and where do they differ from the current LVGL v9 backend?
candidate_symbols: app_install entry candidate: 0x0C2418A8 (Thumb 0x0C2418A9); null-check branch precedes PUSH.W at 0x0C2418AE; caller/export and return ABI remain unapproved
P65 packagemanager app lookup candidate: 0x0C241420; one package-name C-string key, returns an app-record pointer from map 0x3C3CF92C; install/register and unregister paths use the same key
app_launcher_add candidate: 0x0C7EC450; IDA pseudocode shows no explicit arguments; implementation reaches launcher-page insertion
P65 QuickApp removal candidate: 0x0C7EC53C; observed int(app_id), removes a QuickApp launcher record from list head 0x3C3BF9DC; it is not proven to remove app_install records at 0x3C3CF91C
P65 activity page-register candidate: 0x0C2216B4; observed one page-descriptor pointer, registry insertion and callback dispatch; direct caller and app_install relation are unproven

P65 app_install page-object callback candidate: global activity-manager slot 0x3C3CF53C+12 is initialized to ROM Thumb pointer 0x1C1318F1; app_install passes one page descriptor and stores the returned page object; ROM body/prototype is not independently mapped
P65 activity page-unregister candidate: 0x0C22212C; observed one page-descriptor pointer and lifecycle callback dispatch; public call/lifetime contract is unapproved

P65 packagemanager app-unregister/destructor candidate: 0x0C2415C0; one app-record pointer, registry unlink, nested-list cleanup and release via activity-manager slot +16; its +48 page_registry matches the app_install body’s slot +12 registration flow, but direct callers/returned handle remain unknown
launcher_page_insert_icon candidate: 0x0C7F070C; observed one pointer argument for a launcher item
lvx_page_title_create candidate: 0x0C21B2FC; observed five arguments and pointer return
lvx_list_item_set_icon candidate: 0x0C219878; observed two arguments; not equivalent to the required row create/update API
lvx_list_refresh_to_bottom candidate: 0x0C8BD798 / Thumb callable 0x0C8BD799; one list-object pointer, AP trampoline to ROM 0x1C148888; scroll helper only, not row creation/update
P65 LVX list initializer candidate: 0x0C2401D4; caller supplies a native list object and the initializer installs a 40-byte config/callback table

P65 LVX list class-constructor callback candidate: 0x0C23FF40; raw code ignores R0, uses R1 as the list object, initializes state through +1356; shape is consistent with a class constructor callback, but class registration/public entrypoint is unproven
LVGL class-create candidate: 0x0C0D15D4; `(class_descriptor, parent)->object`, allocates from descriptor instance size and attaches to parent/display; not list-specific
LVGL class constructor-dispatch candidate: 0x0C0D16C8; walks class ancestry and calls each class+4 callback as `(class_descriptor, object)`; list descriptor linkage remains unknown
LVGL class destructor-dispatch candidate: 0x0C0D17D4; walks class ancestry and calls each class+8 destructor callback; list destructor callback remains unidentified
P65 LVX list config-copy helper candidate: 0x0C2358C4; code copies 10 words to list+92 after validating required callbacks; function-boundary/public ABI status remains unapproved

P65 LVX list create/config/finalize candidates: 0x0C8BE008 (parent, opaque descriptor) -> object, 0x0C8BEF60 (object, 40-byte callback table), and 0x0C8BEBC0 (object); AP trampolines to ROM 0x1C14885C/0x1C145B00/0x1C147054

P65 internal LVX list reinit candidate: 0x0C236E18; in mode 1 it re-queries count and rebuilds visible rows/extent, called by setup and sub_C236FE8 event handling; not an approved external refresh callable
P65 LVGL object-class create candidate: 0x0C8BEB70 / Thumb 0x0C8BEB71; observed `(class_descriptor, parent)->object` calls, including the P65 `listview` row class descriptor at VMA 0x3C21B55C
P65 LVGL label-child create candidate: 0x0C78BCB4 / Thumb 0x0C78BCB5; one parent pointer, creates a child from label descriptor VMA 0x3C224844
P65 LVGL label text-set candidate: 0x0C78C878 / Thumb 0x0C78C879; int(label, const char *), updates the label-owned text buffer at +52
P65 LVGL event-callback registration candidate: 0x0C8BCE78 / Thumb 0x0C8BCE79; (object, callback, event_code, context), used for click event 7 in row creation
P65 LVGL event-callback removal candidate: 0x0C8BD6D8 / Thumb 0x0C8BD6D9; (object, callback), used before row callback replacement
P65 list-row click handler candidate: 0x0C763C7C; receives an event pointer, dispatches only event code 7, and extracts user context at event+12

P65 all-list callback candidates: key/type 0x0C763B84, row create 0x0C764638, row update 0x0C7644A0, count 0x0C763B34; concrete all_list_view registration/call-site confirms the callback roles but its context uses P65-specific all_list records
P65 LVX row-item constructor-like candidate: 0x0C219454; seven arguments, returns the caller-provided item object after setting up child-object fields; direct public call path is unproven
P65 LVX row-item update candidate: 0x0C2196F8; six arguments, mutates existing item child/style state; relationship to list callback +104 is unproven
lvx_notification_insert_message candidate: 0x0CA60098; observed one pointer argument; not required for initial Manager UI
NuttX open wrapper candidate: 0x0C247EA8 / Thumb callable 0x0C247EA9; int(const char *, int, ...)
NuttX close wrapper candidate: 0x0C244B60 / Thumb callable 0x0C244B61; int(int fd)
NuttX read wrapper candidate: 0x0C2484E4 / Thumb callable 0x0C2484E5; int32_t(int fd, void *buffer, uint32_t count)

CORRECTED after boot-loop report: plain NuttX fd write is 0x0C2497F0 / Thumb 0x0C2497F1; int32_t(int fd, const void *buffer, uint32_t count). The former 0x0C248454/455 candidate is pwrite with an additional stack-passed 64-bit offset; the three-argument binding is invalid. Deployment remains withdrawn; see ../bootloop-incident.md.

callsite_evidence: AP startup copy maps the 0x3C name-data VMA back to cached XIP. The `app_install` name at runtime VMA 0x3C350B00 maps to source/XIP 0x0C4408C4; the `launcher_page_insert_icon` name at 0x3C23F2F4 maps to XIP 0x0C3500B8; the `app_launcher_add` name at 0x3C23E7F0 maps to XIP 0x0C3505B4; and `lvx_page_title_create` at 0x3C2A3300 maps to XIP 0x0C3930C4. Literal-pool references in AP code connect these names to the candidate functions below.

The supplied full OTA archive contains vela_ap/audio/ota/resource/sensor payloads. best1503_vela.py maps vela_ap to XIP 0x0C0C0000 with cached/non-cached aliases 0x2C0C0000/0x280C0000; vela_ota.bin is a separate ARM ELF with PT_LOAD mappings including 0x3C800000 and 0x00200200. The 0x1C... trampoline destinations lie outside the decoded AP mapping and these inspected OTA ELF segments. Here ROM target is shorthand for the address-map inference, not a claim that the user's full package is missing; silicon ROM versus another resident system mapping is not independently verified.

The original IDB misses the entry bytes as code. Raw bytes at 0x0C2418A8 encode `CMP R0,#0; BEQ.W 0x0C2419FA`; 0x0C2419FA is `BX LR`, and the apparent `STRH` at 0x0C2418AC is the second halfword of that 32-bit conditional branch. The code therefore supports 0x0C2418A8 (Thumb pointer 0x0C2418A9) as the app_install entry candidate, with `PUSH.W {R4-R10,LR}` at 0x0C2418AE after the null guard. The body then uses R0/R1/R2 as descriptor/page-array/count, checks duplicate app IDs, allocates/copies 16 descriptor words (64 bytes), duplicates selected strings, inserts into registry 0x3C3CF91C, and registers page pointers. Its copied layout resembles the v9 `firmware_app_descriptor`; however, there are no direct code/data refs to 0x0C2418A8/0x0C2418A9/0x0C2418AE, so external callability/export, return semantics, and page lifetime remain unapproved. The body loads the copied `app_install` name string for logging, identifying the implementation path but not proving its public API.

In the observed app_install page loop, code loads the activity-manager callback at global 0x3C3CF53C+12 (its startup source word at XIP 0x0C4BF30C is ROM Thumb pointer 0x1C1318F1), calls it with each page descriptor pointer in R0, stores the returned page-object pointer in the app record's page_registry array, then maps app id/page id through `sub_C25601C`. This structurally links the app_install body to page registration, but the ROM callback body and public app_install callability remain unresolved.

The app_install body inserts its record into string-keyed map 0x3C3CF92C using descriptor package_name at +8 via `sub_C25601C`; `sub_C2415C0` removes the same key via `sub_C25780C`. Lookup candidate `sub_C241420(package_name)` queries that map and returns its stored app-record pointer. This yields a static record-lookup path for the structurally paired unregister candidate, but no direct AP callers or approved public contract were found.

The app_install active-list scan compares descriptor +16 as a 16-bit app ID; if an active record matches, the routine skips allocation, page registration, and map insertion and exits through its common epilogue. This is a duplicate active-ID no-op, not evidence for duplicate package-name behavior or a useful status return.

A raw 32-bit byte-pattern scan of the loaded IDB found no even/Thumb pointer literals for app_install 0x0C2418A8/0x0C2418A9, lookup 0x0C241420/0x0C241421, unregister 0x0C2415C0/0x0C2415C1, or page-register 0x0C2216B4/0x0C2216B5 and page-unregister 0x0C22212C/0x0C22212D; IDA code/data xrefs to the app_install entry candidates are also absent. The literal at 0x0C241A68 loads runtime name-data address 0x3C350B00 in the function's cleanup/log path, not a demonstrated function-pointer table. Static AP callability is unproven; external ROM or dynamic callers remain possible.

`sub_C2415C0` is not an unconditional final free. When the package-manager state callback at global 0x3C3CF934+56 reports active, it calls page-object release slot +16, unlinks the app record/map, invokes callback +44 with event 4, then either frees the record if a second +56 check reports inactive or links it to deferred list 0x3C3CF920/map 0x3C3CF930 and emits event 28. `sub_C241A78` has no direct callers; its body later removes eligible records from that deferred list, registers their pages via slot +12 and emits event 29, making it a resume/reactivation path rather than a teardown-drain proof. The unregister return value does not establish that page callbacks have drained.

The `activitymanager_page_register` name string maps through startup VMA 0x3C341658 to literal-pool reference 0x0C2217E4; nearby candidate 0x0C2216B4 takes one page pointer, initializes lifecycle/refcount fields and inserts the descriptor into the global page list at 0x3C3CF53C before callback dispatch. It resembles the register half of page unregister but has no direct AP callers or proven app_install linkage.

Page-unregister candidate 0x0C22212C is reached by the `activitymanager_page_unregister` name string. Its code reads lifecycle state at page+40, calls the signal callback at +52 with event codes 6/7/2, indirect-dispatches callbacks at +92/+96, and unlinks page registry links at +64/+68. These offsets resemble the Band 10 page descriptor, but the routine has no direct AP callers and no `app_install` teardown path is linked to it.

Page unregister is not a complete callback-drain proof: `sub_C221C48` increments/decrements page word +36 as a reference count. `sub_C22212C` can reach `sub_C221388`, which synchronously invokes event 8 but, while that refcount is nonzero, queues the page pointer at 0x3C4941A8, increments 0x3C4941D0, sets lifecycle state 4 and returns. `sub_C221E78` later consumes that queue, sends event 22 and calls `sub_C22126C` for state-4 pages; it has no direct AP callers and appears to be scheduler/event driven. Only the zero-refcount path calls `sub_C22126C` immediately, so freeing module callbacks after unregister without proving the queue drained is unsafe.

The `app_launcher_add` name pointer is read in the literal pool preceding 0x0C7EC53C; the associated routine at 0x0C7EC450 obtains an app/launcher object, calls 0x0C7F070C, and updates launcher registries. Code references from 0x0C82FCDC (after an app-registry append) and 0x0C8B3BA8 (an app-launch path) invoke it with no arguments. It therefore appears to be a launcher-refresh helper, unlike the Band 10 v9 backend's `launcher_add(uint16_t)` wrapper; do not reuse that prototype or treat it as a direct add-by-app-ID API.

The NuttX registration trampoline at 0x0C8BD0D0 is a short Thumb stub to ROM 0x1C15A954. P65 driver code calls it with path, a file-operations table, mode 0x1B6, and a private pointer; the HYN/other driver init paths check its return. This matches `register_driver(path,fops,mode,priv)` at the call boundary, but the ROM implementation and a matching unregister API have not been recovered.

`launcher_page_insert_icon` is referenced from the function at 0x0C7EC450 and resolves to 0x0C7F070C. The recovered routine takes one record pointer and uses global launcher state at 0x3C456FA0; this is not the same observed ABI as Band 10's app-ID launcher-add call.

`lvx_page_title_create` resolves to 0x0C21B2FC. Its decompilation and four exact P65 caller sites show five arguments; callers pass `(page/root, title, mode, callback-or-resource, context)`. This arity matches the five-argument typedef in `manager/target/lvgl_v9/canopus_manager_target_lvgl_v9.c`, but callback ownership and the rest of the descriptor ABI still require review.

`lvx_list_item_set_icon` resolves to 0x0C219878 and decompiles as a two-argument item operation. Its P65 implementation reads an item subobject at `item + 84`; the exact Band 10 `.036` evidence in `EVID-UI-001` records the same-named operation accessing `item + 52`, so the list-item layouts are not interchangeable. The P65 strings do not expose the v9 backend's `LVX_LIST_ROW_CREATE`, `LVX_LIST_ROW_UPDATE`, or `LVX_LIST_ROW_TRAILING` names.

P65's LVX list path uses a native callback-driven object, distinct from the v9 row macros. The code at 0x0C2358C4 validates config words at +4/+8/+12/+20, then copies 40 bytes (10 words) into list-object offsets +92..+128; 0x0C2401D4 calls it with built-in ROM Thumb callback pointers: list+96=0x1C15015D, +100=0x1C15034D, +104=0x1C150591, +112=0x1C15016D, +116=0x1C1505E5, +120=0x1C1505F5; +108/+124/+128 are zero in this default table. Internal code proves these callback roles: +96 `(list,index,ctx)->8-bit row-class/cache key`; `sub_C2340C8` reuses a cached row by this byte (cache hit invokes +104, miss invokes +100), +100 `(list,index,ctx)->row object`, +104 `(list,row,index,ctx)->void` update, and +112 `(list,ctx)->item count`. The stock all_list key callback returns 1 for its special final row and 0 for ordinary rows; the host-tested Canopus row adapter returns the semantic node type as its reusable row-class key. In one concrete all-list configuration, +116/+120 are both bound to count-like `(list,ctx)->int` helpers; list-event code also invokes these slots in scroll-boundary branches and ignores their return. Their general semantics remain unknown. +124 replaces row-by-row total-extent measurement in `sub_C235F54`, and +128 supplies a geometry value to scrolling calculations in `sub_C235E6C`; +108 is copied but no use was found in the examined list routines. `sub_C2340C8`, `sub_C235B08`, and `sub_C233414` show the create/update paths. ROM callback bodies are outside this AP database. List class-constructor callback candidate 0x0C23FF40 ignores R0, uses R1 as the object, zeros fields +1340/+1344/+1348/+1352, sets word +1356 to 0x0101, registers a callback through helper 0x0C2570BC, and calls 0x0C255D24 with (object,200,0). This argument shape is consistent with a class constructor callback, but it has no direct AP caller/data xref or embedded AP function pointer, so LVX class registration/public creation remains unproven. Separately, `lv_obj_class_create_obj` string and behavior identify candidate 0x0C0D15D4: it allocates from class descriptor instance-size metadata at +32, stores class/parent pointers, and attaches the object to its parent/display. Candidate 0x0C0D16C8 walks the class chain and invokes +4 constructors as `(class,object)` base-to-derived; candidate 0x0C0D17D4 invokes +8 destructor callbacks in reverse order, after which deletion unlinks/frees the object. Wrapper 0x0C0E1B90 uses generic class descriptor VMA 0x3C1DE5C8 (source/XIP 0x0C2CE38C), whose name pointer resolves to `obj`; descriptor word +32 is 0x34A and the create path decodes its instance size as 0x34 (52 bytes). This is not the `lvx_list` descriptor. No list descriptor link to 0x0C23FF40 or matching +8 destructor was found. Raw AP scans found none of the absolute pointer aliases 0x0C23FF41, 0x2C23FF41, or 0x3C23FF41; the descriptor may be outside AP data or dynamically registered, but neither is proven. Other list code reads +1364, establishing only that the object layout extends at least through that byte; allocator/instance size/destructor are unknown. This recovers internal state and callback conventions, not a supported external API.

A concrete P65 all-list page at `sub_C764170` creates a list widget with ROM trampoline 0x0C8BE008(parent, opaque descriptor 0x3C19D9EC), builds the 40-byte callback table, calls 0x0C8BEF60(list, table), then finalizes through 0x0C8BEBC0(list). The table is `[ctx, sub_C763B84 key/type, sub_C764638 create, sub_C7644A0 update, 0, sub_C763B34 count, sub_C764598, sub_C7645E8, 0, 0]`. `sub_C764638` creates a P65 `listview` class row via ROM class-create trampoline 0x0C8BEB70 with descriptor 0x3C21B55C, then fills its child widgets; The row class descriptor at runtime VMA 0x3C21B55C maps to XIP 0x0C30B320; its +0 base pointer is 0x3C1DE5C8, +20 name pointer 0x3C2852E4 maps to XIP 0x0C3750A8 (`listview`), +32 encoded word 0x4C0 decodes to a 76-byte instance size, and +36 begins `/resource/app/notifications/calendar.bin`. This is a stock notification row class, not the native list-object class; reuse for Manager rows is unverified. It creates labels through 0x0C78BCB4 using descriptor 0x3C224844 (`label`), sets text through 0x0C78C878, and registers click handling through 0x0C8BCE78 with event code 7. The setter replaces/owns a text buffer at label+52. `sub_C7644A0` refreshes that row from the same P65 all_list record context. These callback conventions now have an exact firmware caller, but the callbacks depend on P65 all_list storage and are not directly reusable for Canopus snapshots. The opaque list descriptor, row widget layout, ownership and teardown remain unreviewed.

`sub_C236E18(list,a2,a3)` is an AP-internal list reinitialization path called after setup by `sub_C2401D4` and from `sub_C236FE8`. In list mode 1, it re-queries +112 count, resets visible-range state, rebuilds visible rows through `sub_C2340C8` (+100 create/+104 update), and recalculates extent via `sub_C235F54`; `sub_C236FE8` uses it on some count-change paths. `sub_C236FE8` has no direct AP callers or raw even/Thumb pointer literals, and the callback/event trigger plus public refresh contract remain unproven. Treat this as an internal refresh candidate, not a target callable.

List cache reset candidate `sub_C233200` moves cached row objects to the pool at list+132 via ROM trampoline `sub_C258A1C` (0x0037F61C), then clears the cache array; on pool-entry allocation failure it calls `sub_C257F0C` (0x0037FF28). During row cache insertion, AP trampoline `sub_C2570BC` (0x00388098) registers ROM callback pointer 0x1C143221 for event codes 1/2/3/8. The AP reset path does not itself remove the row's separate click-event-7 callback; ROM pool/destructor behavior is unmapped, so callback binding lifetime across refresh/unload is not proven.

P65 row click callback `sub_C763C7C` reads event code through `sub_C73D8C0(event)`, which returns `(uint16_t *)(event+8) & 0x7FFF`; it accepts code 7, extracts callback user context with `sub_C73D8E4(event)` (word at +12), then publishes a firmware event. The all_list row creator registers `(row, sub_C763C7C, 7, record)` through 0x0C8BCE78; row update first removes that callback via 0x0C8BD6D8(row, callback) and then re-registers with the refreshed record. A Canopus adapter can use a persistent row-binding context and dispatch through its own UI event handler, but that binding must outlive every firmware event reference.

The exact P65 AP contains LVGL source-path strings under `apps/graphics/lvgl/lvgl/src/` plus LVX components including `lvx_widgets/lvx_list.c`. This suggests the v9 backend is worth investigating but does not prove its structure layout, version, or individual function ABIs match P65.

The row-item code has constructor-like candidate 0x0C219454 (`int(item, int, int, int, int, u8, u8)`), which returns the supplied object and conditionally creates child objects at offsets +84/+92/+96 after creating a related child at +88; it does not allocate the outer item. Update candidate 0x0C2196F8 (`int(item, int, int, int, int, char)`) accesses existing fields +84/+88/+92/+96. No direct code/data xrefs link either candidate to the list +100 create or +104 update callback, so this is a row-object candidate only, not recovered callback implementation.

The copied source string `lvx_list_refresh_to_bottom` is at 0x0C342324 (runtime VMA 0x3C252560). The exact caller `sub_C81B2B4` logs that function name and invokes AP Thumb trampoline 0x0C8BD799 (even entry 0x0C8BD798), which jumps to ROM 0x1C148888 with one list-object pointer. It is a scroll-to-bottom helper candidate only; it does not expose list construction or row callbacks.

The `packagemanager_app_unregister` name literal resolves to candidate 0x0C2415C0, which receives an app-record pointer, unlinks a doubly linked record, adjusts counts and releases/requeues nested fields at +48/+52 depending on a manager callback. Its fields resemble the 64-byte app descriptor copy from 0x0C2418AC (registry links +0/+4, app id +16, nested data at +48/+52), and it unlinks a node from the 0x3C3CF91C manager list; the app_install body populates this same +48 page_registry through global activity-manager +12 (ROM 0x1C1318F0), while this unregister candidate iterates those page objects through matching global +16 (ROM 0x1C132368) before unlinking the app record. This strongly pairs record/page teardown with app_install; no direct caller or returned handle is found, and deferred page callbacks remain a separate drain gate. Removal is also partially mapped: `sub_C830114` (`quickapp_unregister_app`) reads an app id at record+16 and calls 0x0C7EC53C. That routine removes a QuickApp entry from list head 0x3C3BF9DC, removes its launcher icon via 0x0C7F077C, and frees the QuickApp record. This differs from `app_install`'s registry at 0x3C3CF91C, so it is not evidence for uninstalling an `app_install` Manager. Separately, `activitymanager_page_unregister` maps to 0x0C22212C, whose code manipulates page lifecycle state and indirect-dispatches page callbacks. No exact callsite ties page unregister to `app_install` teardown, and callback draining/order are unknown; do not call these from Manager unload yet.

The P65 AP includes source strings `vfs/fs_open.c` (file offset 0x2E0BF0), `vfs/fs_close.c` (0x2E0B64), and `vfs/fs_read.c` (0x2E0C10). The low-level file-object open dispatcher is at 0x0C247AE8/0x0C247C64; file-object close is at 0x0C24605C; internal file-object read/write dispatchers are at 0x0C248554/0x0C249854. The fd wrappers are read 0x0C2484E4 and write 0x0C2497F0; 0x0C248454 is pwrite, not ordinary write. This corrects the earlier conflation of fd and file-object boundaries.

The P65 `open` wrapper candidate at 0x0C247EA8 calls the internal file-open routine with the path, flags and optional mode, then allocates a task file descriptor; errors set errno and return -1. Exact P65 AP callers pass pathname strings plus flags/mode, consistent with a POSIX `open` wrapper.

The candidate `close` wrapper at 0x0C244B60 indexes the current task file table using the integer argument, adjusts file references, closes the underlying file when the last reference is released, and returns success/error. It is distinct from internal file-object close at 0x0C24605C.

Raw Thumb disassembly for `read` at 0x0C2484E4 preserves R1 as the buffer and R2 as the byte count, resolves R0 as the fd, and dispatches through the inode read op at offset +8; it returns the byte count or -1 with errno. Plain `write` at 0x0C2497F0 resolves the fd, checks write permission, preserves the supplied buffer/count and dispatches to the inode write op at +12 without seeking. AP callers include 0x0C11E5A8, 0x0C132E88 and 0x0C14B682. The old 0x0C248454 candidate performs save-position/seek/write/restore-position, with LDRD at 0x0C248480 reading the 64-bit offset from entry SP. Exact Thumb emulation reproduces an unintended offset from a poisoned caller stack; this invalidates the prior three-argument write evidence.

The NSH mkdir handler at 0x0C5B0448 splits path components and calls AP trampoline 0x0C8BD850 with `(path, 0x1FF)`; the trampoline jumps to ROM 0x1C157C5C. Its paired runtime string at the handler literal resolves to `mkdir`, supporting a POSIX `mkdir(path, mode)` wrapper; ROM body is not mapped.

The NSH rename handler at 0x0C5B06D4 resolves old/new path strings and calls 0x0C8BDF88 with R0=old path and R1=new path; its paired literal resolves to `rename` and the Thumb stub jumps to ROM 0x1C1587C8. This is consistent with `rename(old,new)`; ROM body is not mapped.
The recursive remove path at 0x0C5AF8A0 calls 0x0C8BC348 with `(path, stat_buffer)`; it reads `st_mode` at buffer+8. Direct stub 0x0C8BC348 jumps to ROM 0x1C15967C, supporting a `stat` candidate.

The same recursive remove path calls 0x0C8BEFD0 with a non-directory path (ROM 0x1C159914) and 0x0C8BBE78 with a directory path after child traversal (ROM 0x1C158B08), consistent with `unlink(path)` and `rmdir(path)` respectively. The associated command handler's copied string resolves to `unlink`.

Directory iteration helpers are implemented in AP: 0x0C4F7884 allocates a 104-byte DIR wrapper and opens the path with flags 3073; 0x0C4F78EC reads up to 98 bytes into its dirent area and returns null at end/error; 0x0C4F78C0 closes the fd and frees the wrapper. These are POSIX-shaped opendir/readdir/closedir candidates, but device semantics are untested.
No `fsync` string or direct AP callsite was recovered; atomic durability required by the generic store cannot be assumed from rename/close alone.

`manager/target/p65/canopus_manager_p65_registry.c` adds a host-tested two-slot envelope for the generic 784-byte CRD1 registry: sequence number, CRC32, inactive-slot write, read-back verification and fallback to the older valid slot; host tests also round-trip Supervisor metadata through the platform hooks. Its slot I/O is injected and no P65 path/syscall is bound; this does not prove filesystem persistence, fsync semantics or power-loss ordering.

The exact AP contains filesystem path literals including `/data`, `/data/ota.zip`, `/data/log`, `/tmp`, and `/system`. These provide plausible roots for a target store/stage area, but do not prove `/data/canopus` exists, is writable, has adequate space, or survives reboot; no device filesystem probes were made.

`manager/target/p65/canopus_manager_p65_rows.c` now provides a firmware-independent bounded flattener from visible semantic nodes to P65 row views; it skips page/list/scroll containers but retains visible descendants, copies row metadata and the string arena into adapter-owned storage (the UI backend's staging snapshot is ephemeral), and validates parent/string extents. It carries generation/key/event/style/layout/value. Its LVGL click callback reads P65 event code/context at +8/+12 and dispatches through `canopus_ui_dispatch_event`, preserving stale-generation checks. Host tests cover flattening, staging-buffer mutation, hidden ancestors, disabled events, non-clicks, stale events, and malformed strings. It remains a host-tested adapter core; no LVX function binding or P65 page integration is included.

`manager/target/p65/canopus_manager_p65_lvx.c` bridges that row storage to the recovered 10-word LVX callback table: +96 row-class/cache key, +100 create, +104 update, +112 count; optional slots remain null. It uses injected create/configure/finalize/refresh/row ops, statically asserts the table is 40 bytes on ARM, and host tests exercise callback wiring and row refresh with fake ops. No firmware address is bound; the actual P65 refresh API and row-widget operations remain unresolved.

`manager/target/p65/canopus_manager_p65_transport.c` exposes a local `canopus_client_io_v1`: `open` validates the canonical `/dev/canopus` path but returns an internal fd sentinel, while read/write forward full CPC2 records to `canopus_supervisor_device_read/write`. Host tests query device and module payloads (including not-found) without a real device node. The generic direct `canopus_supervisor_local_transport` also exists for command-only callers, but has no query payload. These seams avoid `/dev` registration for an in-process Manager client; they do not provide P65 UI bootstrap, module/package platform operations, or external client transport.

The supervisor still needs NuttX `register_driver`/`unregister_driver` if `/dev/canopus` remains an external interface, plus several LVX methods. A P65 AP search found no `unregister_driver` name/string or verified callable; the Band 10 lead 0x0C1B002C is not transferable because that P65 address is inside `sub_C1AFFF4` arithmetic/indexed-store code. This rules out the cross-target address only; the P65 register stub jumps to ROM and an unmapped ROM unregister counterpart remains possible. Open/close/read/write alone do not make the service operational.

The AP payload SHA remains a19b601477569765103eaf468b937bd8026b4d68ffa5c896bde222a79e475858; use raw payload bytes as the firmware identity. The unregister negative scan used a temporary copy of the current database.
unsafe_assumptions: Names recovered through the startup data-copy map and matching behavior do not by themselves prove a callable ABI, ownership, thread safety, or acceptable side effects.

The P65 64-byte app record and page_registry layout resemble the v9 backend. Raw bytes support 0x0C2418A8 (Thumb 0x0C2418A9) as app_install's null-guarded entry candidate, and the body plus 0x0C2415C0 share the registry/page-object release path; 0x0C241420 appears to look up the string-keyed record. No direct AP refs or approved public-call contract establish install/lookup/unregister callability, return semantics, full page descriptor ABI, or duplicate package-name/allocation-error behavior; active duplicate IDs currently short-circuit as a no-op. Page unregister may queue final destruction while +36 is nonzero; the queue consumer has no direct AP callers, so callback drain before module unload is unproven. The separate deferred app-record path at `sub_C241A78` re-registers pages and emits event 29; it is not evidence of final callback drain. `app_launcher_add` is not an app-ID function in the recovered P65 code; app registration may trigger launcher refresh asynchronously, but that relation remains unproven.
P65 `app_launcher_add` and `launcher_page_insert_icon` are not interchangeable with the Band 10 `launcher_add(app_id)` API based on current evidence.

The P65 and Band 10 `.036` `lvx_list_item_set_icon` implementations touch different item offsets (+84 versus +52), and P65's list callbacks reside in a different native object layout; do not transplant the Band 10 list backend layout into P65. The newly recovered callback prototypes are internal evidence only and are not yet safe target callables.

The P65 POSIX-shaped open/close/read/write, mkdir/stat/rename/unlink/rmdir, and directory-iteration wrappers are static AP/ROM-trampoline candidates; ROM bodies are unmapped and no host module or device call has tested them. No fsync callsite was found, so the generic store's crash-durable atomic-rename guarantees cannot be assumed. A register_driver trampoline candidate is found, but its ROM body and matching unregister_driver API remain unreviewed. The QuickApp removal candidate uses a different registry from app_install; the native Manager app/page unregister path remains unknown. A few LVX function-name matches do not provide the full API set required by the Manager. Do not set `CANOPUS_SUP_PLATFORM_COMPLETE=1`, add callables, or build a deployable P65 Manager from these candidates.

The firmware-independent snapshot flattener and injected +96/+100/+104/+112 callback-table bridge are host-tested; the AP now exposes internal list reinit candidate `sub_C236E18`, but its dynamic event trigger/public callability and page ownership are unproven; trace that path and a safe row-cache refresh before binding addresses. The host-only Manager controller now exercises local CPC2 queries, navigation, and ENABLE confirmation through a fake Supervisor, but not P65 app/page lifecycle. Determine whether package-manager/ROM code dynamically resolves or calls the null-guarded app_install candidate at 0x0C2418A8/Thumb 0x0C2418A9; active duplicate IDs currently short-circuit as no-op, but public lookup/unregister ABI and allocation/error results remain unapproved. Establish a real final callback-drain path for page refcount +36 and the 0x3C4941A8 deferred-destroy queue, distinct from the app-record reactivation queue, before rmmod. Search the unmapped ROM for a verified unregister_driver or choose an in-process-only Manager transport that does not register `/dev/canopus`; that alternative still needs target platform file/module I/O, fsync/durability policy, and app bootstrap/thread review.
